note: Sticky is a thin Drupal wrapper around the garand/sticky jQuery plugin. A single admin form (/admin/config/system/sticky, route sticky.sticky_settings_form, permission 'administer sticky') stores ten keys in the sticky.settings config object: selector (default .menu--main), top_spacing (0), bottom_spacing (0), class_name (is-sticky), wrapper_class_name (sticky-wrapper), center (false), get_width_from (''), width_from_wrapper (true), responsive_width (false), z_index (auto). sticky_page_attachments() pushes StickyManager::getJsSettings() into drupalSettings.sticky and attaches the sticky/sticky library, which needs the external file /libraries/sticky/jquery.sticky.js. No config/install defaults and no config schema ship, so the baseline sticky.settings config is ABSENT until saved. All cases are grounded in the sticky.settings config object (read/written with drush); setup/reset write known values and cleanup deletes sticky.settings to restore the absent baseline.

evals.prompt: How do I configure the Drupal 'sticky' module, and in which config object are its settings stored?
evals.expected_output: Configure it at Configuration > System > Sticky (/admin/config/system/sticky, route sticky.sticky_settings_form, permission 'administer sticky'). All settings are stored in the sticky.settings config object.

evals.prompt: Which sticky module setting decides which element on the page becomes sticky, and what is its default value?
evals.expected_output: The 'selector' setting (DOM Selector) is a CSS selector that chooses the element to make sticky; its default is .menu--main. It is global (one selector site-wide).

evals.prompt: The sticky module doesn't seem to do anything after enabling it. What external dependency does it need, and where must it be placed?
evals.expected_output: It wraps the third-party garand/sticky (stickyjs.com) jQuery plugin, which you must download and place at /libraries/sticky/ so that /libraries/sticky/jquery.sticky.js loads. The target element for the selector must also exist in the markup.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the sticky module is configured to make one element stay visible on scroll. Inspect the live configuration and state the CSS/DOM selector of the element that is set to be sticky.
evals.expected_output: The sticky.settings 'selector' is .header-wrapper (drush cget sticky.settings selector).

evals.prompt: The sticky module on this site is configured with a gap between the top of the page and the sticky element. Inspect the live configuration and state the top spacing value (in pixels) that is set.

On this Drupal site, use the sticky module to make the element matching the CSS selector '#footer' the sticky element (so the footer stays visible on scroll). Apply the change to the live site configuration.
evals.expected_output: sticky.settings 'selector' is set to '#footer' (e.g. drush cset sticky.settings selector '#footer', or via the Sticky settings form).

evals.prompt: I want my site header (the element with the CSS class 'site-header', i.e. selector '.site-header') to stick to the top when scrolling, but leave a 30 pixel gap above it so it doesn't cover my admin toolbar. Using the sticky module, set this up on the live site.
evals.expected_output: sticky.settings has selector = '.site-header' and top_spacing = 30 (stored as an integer).
